newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent weaker.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent weaker.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent weaker Tuesday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, trading sources said.
U.S. Census Bureau put mill consumption in May at a seasonally adjusted rate of 10.78 million bales, compred to a revised April figure of 10.91 million bales.
Demand to date was pegged at 10.80 million bales.
"This just shows that consumption is not humming along at an 11.0 million bale pace and we may see a downward adjustment in the consumption figure," Merrill Lynch Judith Ganes, said.
USDA has estimated domestic consumption at 11.0 million bales for the 1996/97 season.
While the data should not weigh too heavily on prices, a slowly developing West Texas crop could pressure the December contract through support at 75.00 cents, traders said.
They pegged the next support level at 74.50 cents a lb with major support seen at 70.00 cents for December delivery.
"It doesn't look pretty," a Lubbock-based trader, said. "The leaves are torn due to sand damage and thrips (insects). The plants need hot and dry weather to put out new leaves."
Hot weather is forecast for West Texas for the next four days. The rain that hit parts of Texas on Monday missed the West Texas cotton areas, Weather Services Corp, said.
USDA said Monday that 54 percent of the cotton crop was in good to excellent condition, compared with 59 percent last year.
NYCE cotton futures settled lower Monday amid brisk speculative selling. But trade buying kept December's head over major support pegged at 75.00 cents.
December closed 0.40 lower at 75.28 cents after trading from 75.80 to 74.97 cents. July ended down 0.61 at 72.09 cents, with the rest 0.40 to 0.15 cent weaker.
An estimated 25,000 lots changed hands on the day.
Cotton merchant William Dunavant issued 182 of the 328 notices issued today, the first notice day for July cotton.
